title: ClaimArbitrage Step 3 hardcodes USDC approval but SYA rewardToken is mutable, causing permanent DoS if rewardToken changes
description: In ClaimArbitrage.unlockCallback(), Step 3 (line 177) approves the immutable USDC address for the SYA claim: IERC20(USDC).approve(address(sya), p.usdcNeeded). However, StableYieldAccumulator.setRewardToken() (lines 468-471) allows the owner to change the reward token. If rewardToken is changed, SYA's claim() will try to safeTransferFrom the new reward token, but ClaimArbitrage only approved USDC. The call reverts permanently. Step 5 (line 208) correctly queries sya.rewardToken() dynamically, proving the developer intended the contract to adapt to rewardToken changes but missed updating Step 3.
impact: Permanent DoS of ClaimArbitrage contract if SYA's rewardToken is ever changed from USDC. The yield consolidation mechanism through ClaimArbitrage stops working. Requires contract redeployment to fix.
attackPath: SYA owner calls setRewardToken() to change rewardToken from USDC to a different token
Any user calls ClaimArbitrage to consolidate yield
Step 3 in unlockCallback() approves USDC (hardcoded) to SYA
SYA's claim() attempts safeTransferFrom on the new rewardToken, not USDC
Transfer reverts because ClaimArbitrage never approved the new rewardToken
ClaimArbitrage is permanently bricked until redeployed
recommendation: Replace the hardcoded USDC approval in Step 3 with a dynamic query: address rt = sya.rewardToken(); IERC20(rt).approve(address(sya), p.usdcNeeded);
